mechanism_narrative: A continued rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the next month raises weekday downtown foot traffic, which lifts RETAIL_REC relative to the prior four weeks. The signal is strongest when RESIDENTIAL eases from elevated stay-at-home levels at the same time.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean after WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise for four consecutive weeks and RESIDENTIAL falls or stays flat.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM moves back above zero change from baseline, nearby discretionary shopping also recovers because routine errands spill over into retail visits. This should push RETAIL_REC upward within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses from negative to non-negative week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week mean for two straight weeks after GROCERY_PHARM turns non-negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL indicates more local leisure and neighborhood circulation, which diverts trips into close-to-home retail and supports higher RETAIL_REC over the following month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite PARKS increasing while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated versus baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp additional drop in TRANSIT below its already depressed level signals renewed restriction or avoidance behavior, which reduces discretionary shopping visits and lowers RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls at least 5 points week-on-week from its current level
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is already far below baseline in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week after a further week-on-week TRANSIT drop of at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both keep rising together, the same population makes more mixed-purpose trips and more impulse retail stops, so RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks. The effect weakens if RESIDENTIAL also rises, implying commuting replacement rather than expanded activity.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 14 days despite concurrent increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A post-weather or school-holiday style shift that lifts PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM while leaving WORKPLACES below baseline channels spending toward local errands rather than destination retail, keeping RETAIL_REC lower than its recent average over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises while WORKPLACES remains below -20 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean even though PARKS is higher and WORKPLACES remains deeply negative.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL continues to fall from its current elevated level while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep recovering, household time at home shrinks and in-person discretionary shopping expands. That combination should lift RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its previous 4-week mean after RESIDENTIAL declines for two straight weeks alongside continuing WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recovery.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-mobility baseline, any further weakening of GROCERY_PHARM together with flat or falling WORKPLACES marks broad demand compression, which spills into discretionary spending and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -5 points and WORKPLACES stays below -25 points
evidence_refs: fact:all major place categories remain below baseline except RESIDENTIAL
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM weakens below -5 points while WORKPLACES stays below -25 points.
